source.text: Τὸν μὲν πρῶτον λόγον ἐποιησάμην περὶ πάντων, ὦ Θεόφιλε, ὧν ἤρξατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς ποιεῖν τε καὶ διδάσκειν ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας ἐντειλάμενος τοῖς ἀποστόλοις διὰ πνεύματος ἁγίου οὓς ἐξελέξατο ἀνελήμφθη·

records.literal_gloss: The indeed first account I made concerning all [things], O Theophilus, which began the Jesus both to do and to teach, \v 2 until which day, having given orders to the apostles through Spirit Holy whom he chose, he was taken up.

en.L: The first account I made, O Theophilus, [was] about all that Jesus began both to do and to teach, \v 2 until the day when, having given orders through [the] Holy Spirit to the apostles whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had chosen, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was taken up.
en.B: Theophilus, the first book I composed told of all that Jesus began both to do and to teach, \v 2 until the day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was taken up. Before that, through the Holy Spirit, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had given orders to the apostles {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had chosen.
en.R: Dear Theophilus, my first book was about everything Jesus began to do and to teach. \v 2 It went on until the day God took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up to heaven. Before {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave orders to the apostles {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had chosen. He did this through the Holy Spirit.

es.L: El primer relato lo hice, oh Teófilo, acerca de todo lo que Jesús comenzó tanto a hacer como a enseñar, \v 2 hasta el día en que, habiendo dado órdenes mediante [el] Espíritu Santo a los apóstoles que había escogido, fue llevado arriba.
es.B: Teófilo, en mi primer libro escribí acerca de todo lo que Jesús comenzó a hacer y a enseñar \v 2 hasta el día en que fue llevado a lo alto. Antes de eso, por medio del Espíritu Santo, había dado órdenes a los apóstoles que había escogido.
es.R: Querido Teófilo: Mi primer libro trató de todo lo que Jesús comenzó a hacer y a enseñar. \v 2 Llegó hasta el día en que Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevó al cielo. Antes de irse, dio órdenes a los apóstoles que había escogido. Lo hizo por medio del Espíritu Santo.

fr.L: J’ai fait le premier récit, ô Théophile, au sujet de tout ce que Jésus a commencé à faire et à enseigner, \v 2 jusqu’au jour où, après avoir donné des ordres par l’Esprit Saint aux apôtres qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait choisis, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été enlevé.
fr.B: Théophile, dans mon premier livre, j’ai raconté tout ce que Jésus a commencé à faire et à enseigner, \v 2 jusqu’au jour où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été enlevé. Auparavant, par l’Esprit Saint, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait donné ses ordres aux apôtres qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait choisis.
fr.R: Cher Théophile, dans mon premier livre, j’ai parlé de tout ce que Jésus a commencé à faire et à enseigner. \v 2 Ce livre va jusqu’au jour où Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a enlevé au ciel. Avant de partir, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a donné des ordres aux apôtres qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait choisis. Il l’a fait par l’Esprit Saint.

sw.L: Masimulizi ya kwanza niliyafanya, ee Theofilo, kuhusu mambo yote ambayo Yesu alianza kufanya na pia kufundisha, \v 2 hadi siku ile ambayo, akiisha kuwapa maagizo kupitia Roho Mtakatifu mitume aliowachagua, alichukuliwa juu.
sw.B: Theofilo, katika kitabu changu cha kwanza niliandika juu ya yote ambayo Yesu alianza kufanya na kufundisha, \v 2 hadi siku alipochukuliwa juu. Kabla ya hapo, kupitia Roho Mtakatifu, alikuwa amewapa maagizo mitume aliowachagua.
sw.R: Mpendwa Theofilo, kitabu changu cha kwanza kilihusu kila kitu ambacho Yesu alianza kufanya na kufundisha. \v 2 Kilieleza mambo hadi siku ile Mungu alipomchukua kwenda mbinguni. Kabla hajaondoka, aliwapa maagizo mitume aliowachagua. Alifanya hivyo kupitia Roho Mtakatifu.

vi.L: Thưa ngài Thê-ô-phi-lơ, bản tường thuật thứ nhất tôi đã viết là về mọi điều Đức Giê-xu đã bắt đầu làm và dạy, \v 2 cho đến ngày {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được cất lên, sau khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nhờ Đức Thánh Linh truyền lệnh cho các sứ đồ mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chọn.
vi.B: Thưa ngài Thê-ô-phi-lơ, trong cuốn sách thứ nhất, tôi đã thuật lại mọi điều Đức Giê-xu đã bắt đầu làm và dạy dỗ, \v 2 cho đến ngày {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được cất lên. Trước đó, qua Đức Thánh Linh, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã truyền lệnh cho các sứ đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chọn.
vi.R: Kính gửi ngài Thê-ô-phi-lơ: Cuốn sách trước của tôi kể về mọi điều Đức Giê-xu đã bắt đầu làm và dạy. \v 2 Sách ấy kể cho đến ngày Đức Chúa Trời đem {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên trời. Trước khi đi, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã truyền lệnh cho các sứ đồ mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chọn. Ngài làm điều đó qua Đức Thánh Linh.

ko.L: 데오빌로 각하, 저는 첫 번째 글에서 예수께서 행하시고 가르치기 시작하신 모든 일에 관하여 썼습니다. \v 2 [그 글은] 그분이 택하신 사도들에게 성령을 통하여 명령하신 뒤에 들려 올라가신 날까지[의 일입니다].
ko.B: 데오빌로 각하, 저는 첫 번째 책에서 예수께서 행하시고 가르치기 시작하신 모든 일을 기록하였습니다. \v 2 그 책은 예수께서 하늘로 들려 올라가신 날까지의 일을 담고 있습니다. 그 전에 예수께서는 성령을 통하여, 택하신 사도들에게 분부하셨습니다.
ko.R: 데오빌로 각하께 드립니다. 저는 첫 번째 책에 예수께서 하시고 가르치기 시작하신 모든 일을 썼습니다. \v 2 그 책은 하나님께서 예수를 하늘로 데려가신 날까지의 이야기입니다. 예수께서는 떠나시기 전에 직접 뽑으신 사도들에게 할 일을 일러 주셨습니다. 성령을 통하여 그렇게 하셨습니다.

decisions.choice: the first account: Luke's earlier book, the Gospel
alternatives: the first of several works still to come
decisions.reason: Luke's Gospel is also written to Theophilus (Luke 1:1-4), and it ends where this book begins, with Jesus taken up near Bethany (Luke 24:50-51). The word for "account" can mean a written work.

decisions.choice: Theophilus: a real person to whom the work is addressed
alternatives: a name for every reader who loves God
decisions.reason: The name means "loved by God" or "friend of God", and some have read it as a name for any believer. But it was an ordinary name of the time, and in Luke 1:3 he is addressed with a title of honor, as a real person would be.

decisions.choice: began to do and to teach: what Jesus started in the Gospel goes on in this book
alternatives: "began" adds nothing: all that Jesus did and taught
decisions.reason: Greek can use "began" with little weight. But Acts goes on to tell what the risen Jesus does through his apostles and the Spirit (2:33, 9:5), so the word likely points forward.

decisions.choice: through the Holy Spirit goes with "having given orders"
alternatives: through the Holy Spirit goes with "whom he had chosen"
decisions.reason: The Greek order allows either. Most naturally, the phrase tells how Jesus gave his orders; Luke 4:1 and 4:14 show Jesus acting in the Spirit's power. The choosing of the Twelve was also done after prayer (Luke 6:12-13).

decisions.choice: was taken up: Jesus taken up into heaven, told in 1:9-11
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Jesus going up into heaven in 1:11 and 1:22. The passive leaves God as the one who takes him up.

decisions.choice: Dear Theophilus; God took him up to heaven
alternatives: O Theophilus; he was taken up
decisions.reason: English does not use "O" to address someone in a letter, so Readable says "Dear". It names God as the one who acts in the passive verb, and says where Jesus was taken, which the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only where Spanish writes a separate pronoun or possessive (lo, le, su, mí)
alternatives: a span for every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves out most of the subject pronouns the English marks ("había escogido", "fue llevado"), and a clitic joined to a verb has nothing separate to capitalise, so the setting covers fewer words than in English. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: Luke's address to Theophilus (1:1-2) in the passé composé at every level; from 1:3 on, narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R), with historic presents kept at Literal
alternatives: passé composé for the narration at every level
decisions.reason: In 1:1-2 Luke speaks to Theophilus in his own voice, as a letter writer would, so French uses the tense of speech, the passé composé, at every level. The story that follows is written narrative: the passé simple suits a careful public reading at Literal and Balanced, and Readable uses the passé composé throughout, as John does. Speeches keep their own tenses at every level. This holds for the whole book.

decisions.choice: l’Esprit Saint (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: "L’Esprit Saint" follows the Greek order and is the form used in John and Hebrews; "le Saint-Esprit" is equally familiar but would make Acts differ from the rest of the translation.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on verb prefixes (aliowachagua, alichukuliwa, alipomchukua); spans only on free pronouns and possessives
alternatives: a span for every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Swahili marks the pronouns for Jesus inside the verb, and a prefix cannot take a capital, so only free pronouns and possessives (yeye, wake, yake) carry the deity_pronoun span, as in Luke. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English through the chapter.

decisions.choice: Theophilus is addressed as "ngài": "Thưa ngài Thê-ô-phi-lơ" (L, B), "Kính gửi ngài Thê-ô-phi-lơ" at the start (R), as in the Vietnamese Luke 1:3
decisions.reason: Acts is addressed to the same man as Luke's Gospel (meaning decision), so he is spoken to in the same way: "ngài", the respectful "you" for a person of standing, lowercase and with no deity_pronoun span. Here the Greek has no title, so none is added.

decisions.choice: "sứ đồ" for apostle and "Đức Thánh Linh" for the Holy Spirit at every level (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: These are the Protestant forms already used in the Vietnamese Gospels and letters. "Thánh Linh" alone stands for "the Spirit" where the Greek does not add "holy"; "Thánh Thần" is the Catholic form and is not used.

decisions.choice: the opening sentence (1:1-2) in 합쇼체, with Luke as "저" and Theophilus as "데오빌로 각하"; the story from 1:3 in the plain written style
decisions.reason: Acts is the second volume to the same Theophilus (meaning decision), so the Korean takes up the courtesy of the Korean Luke 1:1-4, where he is "각하". The Greek here has only the name, without the title of honor of Luke 1:3, but Korean cannot address a man of rank by his bare name in a formal letter. From 1:3 the narrative uses the plain written style of the Korean Gospels (style guide, section 4).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Acts 1-14; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시- ("그분" at Literal), and God and the Holy Spirit likewise
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (style guide, section 7). As in the Korean Luke, respect is carried by the honorific. The apostles and other people take no honorific in the narrative ("베드로가 말했다").

decisions.choice: "들려 올라가다" (L, B); "하나님께서 ... 하늘로 데려가셨다" (R) for the passive "was taken up"
decisions.reason: The same words as the Korean Luke 24:51, where this book's first volume ends. The passive means God took him up (meaning decision), which Readable says, as the English Readable does.

source.text: οἷς καὶ παρέστησεν ἑαυτὸν ζῶντα μετὰ τὸ παθεῖν αὐτὸν ἐν πολλοῖς τεκμηρίοις, δι’ ἡμερῶν τεσσεράκοντα ὀπτανόμενος αὐτοῖς καὶ λέγων τὰ περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: To whom also he presented himself living after the to suffer him by many proofs, through days forty being seen by them and speaking the things concerning the kingdom of the God.

en.L: To them also {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} presented {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} alive after {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} suffering by many convincing proofs, appearing to them through forty days and speaking the things concerning the kingdom of God.
en.B: To them as well {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had shown {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} alive after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} suffered, with many clear proofs, as for forty days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let them see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and told them about the kingdom of God.
en.R: After Jesus had suffered and died, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed the apostles that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was alive again. He gave them many proofs that left no room for doubt. For forty days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} kept appearing to them and talking with them about God's kingdom.

es.L: A ellos también se presentó a {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}} vivo después de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} padecimiento, con muchas pruebas convincentes, dejándose ver por ellos a lo largo de cuarenta días y hablando de las cosas acerca del reino de Dios.
es.B: A ellos también se les había mostrado vivo después de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} sufrimiento, con muchas pruebas claras, pues durante cuarenta días se dejó ver por ellos y les habló del reino de Dios.
es.R: Después de que Jesús sufrió y murió, mostró a los apóstoles que estaba vivo otra vez. Les dio muchas pruebas que no dejaban lugar a dudas. Durante cuarenta días se les apareció una y otra vez y habló con ellos acerca del reino de Dios.

fr.L: À eux aussi {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se présenta vivant après qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} eut souffert, par de nombreuses preuves décisives, se faisant voir d’eux pendant quarante jours et parlant des choses qui concernent le royaume de Dieu.
fr.B: À eux aussi, après avoir souffert, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’était montré vivant, avec bien des preuves évidentes : pendant quarante jours, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’était laissé voir par eux et leur avait parlé du royaume de Dieu.
fr.R: Jésus a souffert et il est mort. Après cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a montré aux apôtres qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était de nouveau vivant. Il leur a donné beaucoup de preuves qui ne laissaient aucun doute. Pendant quarante jours, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur est apparu souvent et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a parlé du royaume de Dieu.

sw.L: Kwao pia alijionyesha akiwa hai baada ya mateso {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, kwa ithibati nyingi, akiwatokea katika siku arobaini na kusema mambo yahusuyo ufalme wa Mungu.
sw.B: Kwao pia alikuwa amejionyesha kwamba yu hai baada ya mateso {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, kwa ithibati nyingi zilizo wazi, kwa kuwa kwa siku arobaini aliwatokea na kuwaeleza habari za ufalme wa Mungu.
sw.R: Baada ya Yesu kuteswa na kufa, aliwaonyesha mitume kwamba yu hai tena. Aliwapa ithibati nyingi zisizoacha nafasi ya shaka. Kwa siku arobaini aliendelea kuwatokea na kuzungumza nao kuhusu ufalme wa Mungu.

vi.L: Với họ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng đã tỏ mình ra là đang sống sau khi chịu khổ, bằng nhiều bằng chứng chắc chắn; trong bốn mươi ngày {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hiện ra với họ và nói về những điều thuộc về vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Sau khi chịu khổ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã cho họ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang sống, với nhiều bằng chứng rõ ràng. Trong bốn mươi ngày, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hiện ra cho họ thấy và nói với họ về vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Sau khi Đức Giê-xu chịu khổ và chết, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho các sứ đồ thấy rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã sống lại. Ngài cho họ nhiều bằng chứng, khiến họ không còn nghi ngờ gì nữa. Suốt bốn mươi ngày, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhiều lần hiện ra với họ và nói chuyện với họ về vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그분은 고난을 받으신 뒤에 많은 확실한 증거로 그들에게 자신이 살아 계심을 보이셨다. 사십 일 동안 그들에게 나타나 보이시며 하나님 나라에 관한 일들을 말씀하셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 고난을 받으신 뒤에, 여러 가지 확실한 증거로 그들에게 자신이 살아 계신 것을 보여 주셨다. 사십 일 동안 그들에게 나타나셔서 하나님 나라에 관하여 말씀하셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 고난을 받고 돌아가셨다. 그 뒤에 예수께서는 사도들에게 자신이 다시 살아나신 것을 보여 주셨다. 아무도 의심할 수 없는 증거를 많이 보여 주셨다. 예수께서는 사십 일 동안 여러 번 그들에게 나타나셔서, 하나님 나라에 관하여 이야기해 주셨다.

decisions.choice: convincing proofs: signs that settle the matter
decisions.reason: The word was used for evidence that decides a question beyond doubt. Luke 24:36-43 shows such proofs: the risen Jesus is touched, and eats in front of them.

decisions.choice: after his suffering: after his death on the cross
alternatives: the pain before his death only
decisions.reason: In Luke and Acts, "suffer" said of the Messiah takes in his death (Luke 24:26, 24:46; Acts 3:18).

decisions.choice: through forty days: he appeared again and again over that time
alternatives: he stayed with them without a break for forty days
decisions.reason: The participle "being seen" describes appearances that came and went. In 13:31 Paul says he "appeared for many days" to those who came up with him from Galilee.

decisions.choice: the kingdom of God: God's rule, the theme that opens and closes Acts
decisions.reason: Acts ends with Paul proclaiming the kingdom of God in Rome (28:31). The apostles' question in 1:6 shows they heard him speaking of God's promised reign.

decisions.choice: Jesus; the apostles; suffered and died
alternatives: he; to them; after his suffering
decisions.reason: Readable names the people the pronouns point to, and says that the suffering included his death, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: le royaume de Dieu at every level (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the whole New Testament. "Le règne" says the rule more than the realm (m4), but "le royaume" is the familiar term and keeps the thread that opens and closes Acts; Readable keeps it too, as the English does.

decisions.choice: ithibati
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a proof that settles the matter (meaning decision m1). "Ithibati" is a proof that can be counted, so it can be "many"; "ushahidi" would blur it with the witness and testimony words ("shahidi", "ushuhuda") that Acts uses for the apostles.

decisions.choice: "vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời" for the kingdom of God at every level, as in the Vietnamese Luke
decisions.reason: The meaning decision calls this the theme that opens and closes Acts, so it keeps the wording of Luke's Gospel here and in 28:31. Readable keeps it too, where the English Readable says "God's kingdom".

decisions.choice: "확실한 증거" (L, B), "아무도 의심할 수 없는 증거" (R); "하나님 나라" at every level
decisions.reason: Convincing proofs settle the matter (meaning decision), so Korean adds "확실한". "하나님 나라" is the form of the Korean Luke for the kingdom of God, God's rule.

source.text: καὶ συναλιζόμενος παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων μὴ χωρίζεσθαι, ἀλλὰ περιμένειν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ πατρὸς ἣν ἠκούσατέ μου·

records.literal_gloss: And eating together he ordered them from Jerusalem not to depart, but to wait for the promise of the Father which you heard of me.

en.L: And while eating together [with them], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ordered them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father, "which you heard from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shared a meal with them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} charged them not to go away from Jerusalem but to wait there for what the Father had promised: "the promise you heard about from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was eating a meal with them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them, "Do not leave Jerusalem. Stay here and wait for what the Father promised to send. I have told you about this.

es.L: Y mientras comía con [ellos], les ordenó que no se alejaran de Jerusalén, sino que esperaran la promesa del Padre, «que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.B: Mientras compartía una comida con ellos, les mandó que no se fueran de Jerusalén, sino que esperaran allí lo que el Padre había prometido: «la promesa de la que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} hablar.
es.R: Mientras comía con ellos, les dijo: «No {{plural_you:se vayan|os vayáis}} de Jerusalén. {{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} aquí y {{plural_you:esperen|esperad}} lo que el Padre prometió enviar. Ya {{plural_you:les|os}} he hablado de esto.

fr.L: Et, mangeant avec [eux], {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur ordonna de ne pas s’éloigner de Jérusalem, mais d’attendre la promesse du Père, « que vous avez entendue de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.B: Comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} partageait un repas avec eux, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur recommanda de ne pas quitter Jérusalem, mais d’y attendre ce que le Père avait promis : « la promesse dont vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez entendu parler.
fr.R: Pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prenait un repas avec eux, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a dit : « Ne quittez pas Jérusalem. Restez ici et attendez ce que le Père a promis d’envoyer. Je vous en ai parlé.

sw.L: Na alipokuwa akila pamoja [nao], aliwaagiza wasiondoke Yerusalemu, bali waingoje ahadi ya Baba, "ambayo mliisikia kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}.
sw.B: Alipokuwa akila chakula pamoja nao, aliwaamuru wasiondoke Yerusalemu, bali wangoje huko kile ambacho Baba aliahidi: "ile ahadi ambayo mmenisikia nikiinena.
sw.R: Alipokuwa akila pamoja nao, aliwaambia, "Msiondoke Yerusalemu. Kaeni hapa mngoje kile ambacho Baba aliahidi kutuma. Nimekwisha kuwaambia habari zake.

vi.L: Và khi ăn chung [với họ], {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} truyền cho họ đừng rời khỏi Giê-ru-sa-lem, nhưng hãy chờ đợi lời hứa của Cha, "là điều các con đã nghe {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói.
vi.B: Trong một bữa ăn với họ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dặn họ đừng rời khỏi Giê-ru-sa-lem, nhưng hãy ở đó chờ đợi điều Cha đã hứa: "là lời hứa các con đã nghe {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói đến.
vi.R: Trong khi đang ăn với họ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dặn họ: "Đừng rời khỏi Giê-ru-sa-lem. Hãy ở lại đây và chờ đợi điều Cha đã hứa sẽ ban. Ta đã nói với các con về điều này rồi.

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 [그들과] 함께 음식을 드시면서, 그들에게 예루살렘을 떠나지 말고 아버지의 약속을 기다리라고 명령하셨다. "[그것은] 너희가 나에게서 들은 것이다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 그들과 함께 음식을 잡수시면서, 예루살렘을 떠나지 말고 거기서 아버지께서 약속하신 것을 기다리라고 그들에게 분부하셨다. "그것은 너희가 나에게서 들은 약속이다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 그들과 함께 음식을 잡수시면서 말씀하셨다. "예루살렘을 떠나지 마라. 여기 머물면서 아버지께서 보내 주시겠다고 약속하신 것을 기다려라. 내가 이 일에 관하여 너희에게 말해 주었다.

decisions.choice: eating together: sharing a meal with them
decisions.reason: The word is rare. It can be read as "sharing salt", that is, eating together, and Acts 10:41 says the apostles "ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead" (also Luke 24:41-43). A very similar word means "to stay with", and others take it as "assembling".

decisions.choice: which you heard from me: Luke slips from reporting Jesus's words into quoting them
decisions.reason: The sentence begins as reported speech ("he ordered them") and moves to Jesus's own words, so "me" is Jesus. Greek writers often slide from one to the other. The quotation runs to the end of 1:5.

decisions.choice: the promise of the Father: the Holy Spirit, whom the Father promised to give
decisions.reason: 1:5 names what is promised, and Peter says in 2:33 that Jesus received "the promise of the Holy Spirit" from the Father and poured it out. In Luke 24:49 Jesus says "I am sending the promise of my Father upon you".

decisions.choice: the quotation opens at "which you heard" (B), and at the order not to leave (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced opens the quotation where the Greek turns to Jesus's own words. Readable turns the whole order into direct speech, which is easier to follow.

decisions.choice: what the Father promised to send
decisions.reason: "To send" makes the promise concrete: the Father is sending the Spirit (Luke 24:49).

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}}; « » for the quotation
decisions.reason: Every plural "you", pronoun or verb, is the plural_you setting: the ustedes form (Latin America) by default, the vosotros form (Spain) as the alternative; English has no such choice. Spanish quotations take « », opening where the English opens its quotation (meaning decision m2). The same through the book.

decisions.choice: Jesus says "Ta" (with the setting span in mid-sentence) and calls the apostles "các con"; the narrator calls him "Ngài" (1:4-8)
decisions.reason: The forms of the Vietnamese Luke, which the same writer continues here: the risen Jesus speaks to his apostles as a teacher to his disciples.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to the apostles in 해라체 ("너희", "기다려라"), as in the Korean Gospels; the quotation opens where the English opens it
alternatives: the order reported indirectly at every level
decisions.reason: Luke slips from reporting into quoting (meaning decision); Korean can do the same, and Jesus's words take the speech level of the Korean Luke. "잡수시다" is the honorific for eating.

source.text: ὅτι Ἰωάννης μὲν ἐβάπτισεν ὕδατι, ὑμεῖς δὲ ἐν πνεύματι βαπτισθήσεσθε ἁγίῳ οὐ μετὰ πολλὰς ταύτας ἡμέρας.

records.literal_gloss: For John indeed baptized with water, you but in Spirit will be baptized Holy not after many these days.

en.L: For John baptized with water, but you will be baptized in [the] Holy Spirit not many days after these."
en.B: For John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit before many days have passed."
en.R: John baptized people with water. But in only a few days, God will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."

es.L: Porque Juan bautizó con agua, pero {{plural_you:ustedes serán bautizados|vosotros seréis bautizados}} en [el] Espíritu Santo no muchos días después de estos».
es.B: Porque Juan bautizó con agua, pero {{plural_you:ustedes serán bautizados|vosotros seréis bautizados}} con el Espíritu Santo dentro de no muchos días».
es.R: Juan bautizaba a la gente con agua. Pero dentro de pocos días Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} bautizará con el Espíritu Santo».

fr.L: Car Jean a baptisé avec de l’eau, mais vous, vous serez baptisés dans l’Esprit Saint, pas beaucoup de jours après ceux-ci. »
fr.B: Car Jean a baptisé avec de l’eau, mais vous, vous serez baptisés dans l’Esprit Saint d’ici peu de jours. »
fr.R: Jean a baptisé les gens avec de l’eau. Mais dans quelques jours seulement, Dieu vous baptisera dans l’Esprit Saint. »

sw.L: Kwa kuwa Yohana alibatiza kwa maji, lakini ninyi mtabatizwa katika Roho Mtakatifu si siku nyingi baada ya hizi."
sw.B: Kwa maana Yohana alibatiza kwa maji, lakini ninyi mtabatizwa kwa Roho Mtakatifu kabla siku nyingi hazijapita."
sw.R: Yohana aliwabatiza watu kwa maji. Lakini baada ya siku chache tu, Mungu atawabatiza ninyi kwa Roho Mtakatifu."

vi.L: Vì Giăng đã làm báp-têm bằng nước, nhưng các con sẽ chịu báp-têm trong Đức Thánh Linh, không lâu sau những ngày này."
vi.B: Giăng đã làm báp-têm bằng nước, nhưng chẳng bao lâu nữa, các con sẽ chịu báp-têm bằng Đức Thánh Linh."
vi.R: Giăng làm báp-têm cho người ta bằng nước. Nhưng chỉ ít ngày nữa thôi, Đức Chúa Trời sẽ làm báp-têm cho các con bằng Đức Thánh Linh."

ko.L: 요한은 물로 세례를 주었으나, 너희는 이제 며칠 지나지 않아 성령으로 세례를 받을 것이다."
ko.B: 요한은 물로 세례를 주었지만, 너희는 머지않아 성령으로 세례를 받을 것이다."
ko.R: 요한은 사람들에게 물로 세례를 주었다. 그러나 며칠 지나지 않아 하나님께서 너희에게 성령으로 세례를 주실 것이다."

decisions.choice: John's own words, now spoken by Jesus: water, then the Spirit
decisions.reason: John the Baptist said he baptized with water but the one coming after him would baptize with the Holy Spirit (Luke 3:16). Peter recalls this saying of Jesus in 11:16.

decisions.choice: in the Holy Spirit: the Spirit is poured out like the water they are dipped in
alternatives: by the Holy Spirit as the one who baptizes
decisions.reason: The phrase stands next to "with water" and works the same way: the Spirit is what they will be immersed in. In 2:17-18, 2:33 the Spirit is "poured out".

decisions.choice: not many days after these: soon
decisions.reason: Greek often says "not many" for "few". The Spirit comes at Pentecost (2:1), about ten days after the forty days of 1:3.

decisions.choice: God will baptize you
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who acts in the passive verb. Peter says in 2:33 that Jesus, having received the Spirit from the Father, poured it out; naming God keeps to what the Greek implies without choosing between them.

decisions.choice: baptisés dans l’Esprit Saint
decisions.reason: "Dans" keeps the picture of the meaning note (m2): they are immersed in the Spirit as in the water. "Par" would make the Spirit the one who baptizes, and "du Saint-Esprit" is old-fashioned.

decisions.choice: katika Roho Mtakatifu (L); kwa Roho Mtakatifu (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek "in", the picture of being dipped in the Spirit as in water (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable use "kwa", as with "kwa maji" just before, the usual Swahili for the means of baptism.

decisions.choice: "chịu báp-têm trong Đức Thánh Linh" (L); "bằng Đức Thánh Linh" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording of John's saying in the Vietnamese Luke 3:16, which Jesus now takes up (meaning decision). "làm báp-têm" is settled for baptize; "chịu báp-têm" is its passive, as in Luke 3:21.

decisions.choice: "세례" at every level; "이제 며칠 지나지 않아" (L), "머지않아" (B) for "not many days after these"
decisions.reason: "세례" is the word of the Korean Gospels (Luke 3:16). Literal says "not many days" in the natural Korean way; the sense is soon (meaning decision).

source.text: Οἱ μὲν οὖν συνελθόντες ἠρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Κύριε, εἰ ἐν τῷ χρόνῳ τούτῳ ἀποκαθιστάνεις τὴν βασιλείαν τῷ Ἰσραήλ;

records.literal_gloss: Those indeed therefore having come together were asking him saying, Lord, if at the time this you are restoring the kingdom to the Israel?

en.L: So those who had come together were asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Lord, at this time are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} restoring the kingdom to Israel?"
en.B: When they had gathered, they kept asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, is this the time when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will restore the kingdom to Israel?"
en.R: So when the apostles met with Jesus, they asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, is this the time {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will give the kingdom back to Israel?"

es.L: Entonces los que se habían reunido {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaban, diciendo: «Señor, ¿es en este tiempo cuando restauras el reino a Israel?».
es.B: Una vez reunidos, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaban con insistencia: «Señor, ¿es este el momento en que vas a restaurar el reino a Israel?».
es.R: Cuando los apóstoles se reunieron con Jesús, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «Señor, ¿es este el momento en que vas a devolverle el reino a Israel?».

fr.L: Ceux donc qui s’étaient réunis {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interrogeaient, disant : « Seigneur, est-ce en ce temps-ci que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} rétablis le royaume pour Israël ? »
fr.B: Une fois réunis, ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demandaient avec insistance : « Seigneur, est-ce maintenant que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} vas rétablir le royaume pour Israël ? »
fr.R: Alors, quand les apôtres se sont retrouvés avec Jésus, ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont demandé : « Seigneur, est-ce maintenant que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} vas rendre le royaume à Israël ? »

sw.L: Basi wale waliokusanyika walikuwa wakimwuliza, wakisema, "Bwana, je, ni wakati huu unaourejesha ufalme kwa Israeli?"
sw.B: Walipokuwa wamekusanyika, waliendelea kumwuliza, "Bwana, je, huu ndio wakati utakaourejesha ufalme kwa Israeli?"
sw.R: Mitume walipokutana na Yesu, walimwuliza, "Bwana, je, sasa ndio wakati utakaoirudishia Israeli ufalme wake?"

vi.L: Vậy những người đã nhóm lại cứ hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Lạy Chúa, có phải trong lúc này Chúa khôi phục vương quốc cho Y-sơ-ra-ên không?"
vi.B: Khi đã nhóm lại, họ cứ hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Lạy Chúa, có phải đây là lúc Chúa sẽ khôi phục vương quốc cho Y-sơ-ra-ên không?"
vi.R: Khi các sứ đồ nhóm lại với Đức Giê-xu, họ hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Lạy Chúa, có phải bây giờ Chúa sẽ trả lại vương quốc cho Y-sơ-ra-ên không?"

ko.L: 그래서 함께 모인 사람들이 그분께 여쭈었다. "주님, 주님께서 이스라엘에게 나라를 회복하시는 때가 바로 이때입니까?"
ko.B: 사도들이 함께 모였을 때에 예수께 거듭 여쭈었다. "주님, 이스라엘에게 나라를 다시 세워 주실 때가 지금입니까?"
ko.R: 사도들은 예수와 함께 모였을 때에 이렇게 여쭈었다. "주님, 이제 이스라엘에게 나라를 되돌려 주시려는 것입니까?"

decisions.choice: those who had come together: the apostles, gathered with Jesus
decisions.reason: "So" ties the question to what Jesus has just said about the Spirit. The place seems to be the Mount of Olives, from which they return in 1:12.

decisions.choice: "if" here opens a direct question
decisions.reason: In the Greek of this time "if" can introduce a direct question, as in Luke 13:23 and Acts 19:2.

decisions.choice: restore the kingdom to Israel: give Israel back its own kingdom under God's king
decisions.reason: The hope is for the throne of David to be set up again (Luke 1:32-33) and Israel set free (Luke 24:21). Jesus does not deny the hope; he refuses to give a date (1:7) and turns them to their task (1:8).

decisions.choice: were asking: they asked more than once, or pressed the question
decisions.reason: The tense describes an ongoing action.

decisions.choice: the apostles met with Jesus; give the kingdom back
alternatives: those who had come together; restore the kingdom
decisions.reason: Readable names those present and says "restore" in common words.

decisions.choice: "Lạy Chúa", and "Chúa" for "you", with no setting span
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Luke, disciples who call Jesus Lord use "Chúa" for "you"; it is a word of address and takes no span, where the English marks "You".

decisions.choice: the apostles speak to Jesus in 합쇼체 with "주님" ("여쭈었다", "-입니까?"), and repeat "주님" where English has "you"
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Luke, people speak to Jesus in the formal polite style, and Korean names him by his title rather than use a pronoun.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Οὐχ ὑμῶν ἐστιν γνῶναι χρόνους ἢ καιροὺς οὓς ὁ πατὴρ ἔθετο ἐν τῇ ἰδίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ, ἀλλὰ λήμψεσθε δύναμιν ἐπελθόντος τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἔσεσθέ μου μάρτυρες ἔν τε Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ ἐν πάσῃ τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ καὶ Σαμαρείᾳ καὶ ἕως ἐσχάτου τῆς γῆς.

records.literal_gloss: He said but to them, Not yours it is to know times or seasons which the Father set in the own authority, \v 8 but you will receive power having come the Holy Spirit upon you, and you will be of me witnesses in both Jerusalem and in all the Judea and Samaria and to [the] end of the earth.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "It is not yours to know times or seasons which the Father has set by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own authority, \v 8 but you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witnesses both in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to [the] end of the earth."
en.B: He answered them, "Times and seasons that the Father has fixed by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own authority are not yours to know. \v 8 But when the Holy Spirit comes upon you, you will receive power, and you will bear witness to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in Jerusalem, through all Judea and Samaria, and out to the farthest end of the earth."
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Those times and dates are not for you to know. The Father has set them, and they are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} to decide. \v 8 But the Holy Spirit will come on you, and you will receive power. Then you will tell people about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You will tell them in Jerusalem, in all of Judea and Samaria, and in the farthest places on earth."

es.L: Pero les dijo: «No es {{plural_you:cosa de ustedes|cosa vuestra}} conocer tiempos o momentos que el Padre fijó con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia autoridad, \v 8 sino que {{plural_you:recibirán|recibiréis}} poder cuando el Espíritu Santo venga sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} testigos tanto en Jerusalén como en toda Judea y Samaria, y hasta [el] extremo de la tierra».
es.B: Él les respondió: «No {{plural_you:les|os}} corresponde saber los tiempos ni los momentos que el Padre ha fijado con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia autoridad. \v 8 Pero cuando el Espíritu Santo venga sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:recibirán|recibiréis}} poder, y {{plural_you:darán|daréis}} testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} en Jerusalén, por toda Judea y Samaria, y hasta el último rincón de la tierra».
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «Esas fechas y esos momentos no son {{plural_you:cosa de ustedes|cosa vuestra}}. El Padre los ha fijado, y a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le toca decidirlos. \v 8 Pero el Espíritu Santo vendrá sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y {{plural_you:recibirán|recibiréis}} poder. Entonces {{plural_you:hablarán|hablaréis}} de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} a la gente. Lo {{plural_you:harán|haréis}} en Jerusalén, en toda Judea y Samaria, y en los lugares más lejanos de la tierra».

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Ce n’est pas à vous de connaître les temps ou les moments que le Père a fixés de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} propre autorité, \v 8 mais vous recevrez une puissance quand l’Esprit Saint sera venu sur vous, et vous serez {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} témoins à Jérusalem, et dans toute la Judée et la Samarie, et jusqu’à l’extrémité de la terre. »
fr.B: Il leur répondit : « Les temps et les moments que le Père a fixés de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} propre autorité, il ne vous appartient pas de les connaître. \v 8 Mais quand l’Esprit Saint viendra sur vous, vous recevrez une puissance, et vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rendrez témoignage à Jérusalem, dans toute la Judée et la Samarie, et jusqu’au bout de la terre. »
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Ces temps et ces dates, vous n’avez pas à les connaître. C’est le Père qui les a fixés, et c’est à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} d’en décider. \v 8 Mais l’Esprit Saint viendra sur vous, et vous recevrez une puissance. Alors vous parlerez de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aux gens. Vous le ferez à Jérusalem, dans toute la Judée et la Samarie, et jusque dans les endroits les plus lointains de la terre. »

sw.L: Akawaambia, "Si yenu kujua vipindi au nyakati ambazo Baba ameziweka kwa mamlaka {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} mwenyewe, \v 8 bali mtapokea nguvu, Roho Mtakatifu akiwa amekuja juu yenu, nanyi mtakuwa mashahidi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} katika Yerusalemu, na kote Uyahudi na Samaria, na hadi mwisho wa dunia."
sw.B: Akawajibu, "Vipindi na nyakati ambazo Baba amezipanga kwa mamlaka {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} si mambo yenu kuyajua. \v 8 Lakini Roho Mtakatifu atakapowajia, mtapokea nguvu, nanyi mtanishuhudia huko Yerusalemu, kote Uyahudi na Samaria, hadi miisho ya dunia."
sw.R: Yesu akawaambia, "Si kwa ajili yenu kujua nyakati hizo na tarehe hizo. Baba ndiye aliyeziweka, na ni juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kuamua. \v 8 Lakini Roho Mtakatifu atakuja juu yenu, nanyi mtapokea nguvu. Ndipo mtawaambia watu habari {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}. Mtawaambia huko Yerusalemu, kote Uyahudi na Samaria, na mpaka sehemu za mbali kabisa duniani."

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Việc biết thời gian hay thời điểm mà Cha đã định bởi quyền riêng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không phải là việc của các con; \v 8 nhưng các con sẽ nhận lãnh quyền năng khi Đức Thánh Linh ngự xuống trên các con, và các con sẽ làm nhân chứng của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tại Giê-ru-sa-lem, khắp cả Giu-đê và Sa-ma-ri, cho đến tận cùng trái đất."
vi.B: Ngài đáp: "Thời gian và thời điểm mà Cha đã ấn định bằng quyền riêng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, các con không được biết. \v 8 Nhưng khi Đức Thánh Linh ngự xuống trên các con, các con sẽ nhận được quyền năng và sẽ làm chứng về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tại Giê-ru-sa-lem, khắp miền Giu-đê và Sa-ma-ri, cho đến tận cùng trái đất."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Các con không được biết khi nào những việc ấy xảy ra. Cha đã định thời gian ấy, và chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} quyết định. \v 8 Nhưng Đức Thánh Linh sẽ ngự xuống trên các con, và các con sẽ nhận được quyền năng. Rồi các con sẽ đi nói cho mọi người biết về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Các con sẽ nói tại Giê-ru-sa-lem, khắp miền Giu-đê và Sa-ma-ri, và đến những nơi xa nhất trên trái đất."

ko.L: 그분이 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "아버지께서 자기 권한으로 정해 두신 시간이나 때는 너희가 알 바가 아니다. \v 8 그러나 성령께서 너희에게 임하시면, 너희는 능력을 받을 것이다. 그리고 너희는 예루살렘과 온 유대와 사마리아에서, 그리고 땅끝까지 나의 증인이 될 것이다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "아버지께서 자기 권한으로 정하신 시간이나 때는 너희가 알 일이 아니다. \v 8 그러나 성령께서 너희에게 내려오시면, 너희는 능력을 받을 것이다. 그리고 너희는 예루살렘과 온 유대와 사마리아와 땅끝에 이르기까지 나를 증언할 것이다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "그때가 언제인지는 너희가 알 수 없다. 그것은 아버지께서 정하시는 일이다. \v 8 그러나 성령께서 너희에게 오시면, 너희는 능력을 받을 것이다. 그러면 너희는 사람들에게 나에 관하여 알릴 것이다. 예루살렘에서, 온 유대와 사마리아에서, 그리고 땅의 가장 먼 곳까지 가서 알릴 것이다."

decisions.choice: times or seasons: how long, and at what set moment
alternatives: two words for the same thing
decisions.reason: The first word is time as a span, the second a fitting or appointed time. Together they mean "when", as in 1 Thessalonians 5:1.

decisions.choice: but: in place of knowing the date, they are given power for a task
decisions.reason: "But" turns from what is not theirs (the timing) to what will be theirs (power from the Spirit).

decisions.choice: witnesses: people who saw and now tell what they saw
alternatives: martyrs, people who die for their faith
decisions.reason: In Acts a witness has seen the risen Jesus and speaks of it (1:22, 2:32, 10:39-41). The later sense "martyr" grew from this word, but it is not the meaning here.

decisions.choice: my witnesses: they belong to Jesus and speak about him
alternatives: only witnesses who belong to him
decisions.reason: The Greek "of me" can mean either; both are true in Acts, where the apostles are sent by Jesus and speak of him.

decisions.choice: to the end of the earth: the words of Isaiah 49:6, and the path Acts follows
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 49:6 God's servant is made a light for the nations, "that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth"; Paul quotes it in 13:47. Acts tells the story in this order: Jerusalem (chapters 1-7), Judea and Samaria (8-9), then the nations as far as Rome.

decisions.choice: you will bear witness to me
decisions.reason: Balanced says it with a verb, which keeps both senses of "of me": they are his, and they speak of him.

decisions.choice: you will tell people about me; they are his to decide
alternatives: you will be my witnesses; by his own authority
decisions.reason: Readable says what a witness does, and says "authority" in plain words.

decisions.choice: Uyahudi
decisions.reason: The book-wide name for Judea in these drafts, as in John: "Uyahudi" is the land of the Jews in everyday Swahili, while "Yudea" copies the Greek and is less familiar.

decisions.choice: "nhân chứng của Ta" (L); "làm chứng về Ta" (B); "nói cho mọi người biết về Ta" (R)
decisions.reason: "nhân chứng" and "làm chứng" are the style guide's words for witness; Literal keeps the possessive (meaning decision: they belong to Jesus), Balanced turns it into the verb, as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: "증인" (L), "증언하다" (B), "알리다" (R); "땅끝" (L, B), "땅의 가장 먼 곳" (R)
decisions.reason: The witnesses saw and now tell what they saw (meaning decision); "증인" and "증언하다" are the words of the Korean John and Luke 24:48. Balanced and Readable follow the English in making it a verb.

decisions.choice: the honorific for the Holy Spirit ("성령께서 ... 임하시면"), through Acts
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Luke 12:12, the Holy Spirit is spoken of as God is, with "께서" and -시-.

source.text: καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν βλεπόντων αὐτῶν ἐπήρθη καὶ νεφέλη ὑπέλαβεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And these things having said, watching them, he was lifted up, and a cloud took up him from the eyes of them.

en.L: And having said these things, as they were watching, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was lifted up, and a cloud took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up from their eyes.
en.B: With these words said, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was lifted up as they watched, and a cloud received {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that their eyes could no longer see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: After Jesus said this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was lifted up into the sky while they watched. Then a cloud covered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they could not see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} anymore.

es.L: Y habiendo dicho estas cosas, mientras ellos miraban, fue elevado, y una nube {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} tomó de delante de sus ojos.
es.B: Dicho esto, fue elevado mientras ellos miraban, y una nube {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} recibió, y ya no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} pudieron ver.
es.R: Después de decir esto, Jesús fue elevado hacia el cielo mientras ellos miraban. Luego una nube {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} cubrió, y ya no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vieron más.

fr.L: Et ayant dit cela, tandis qu’ils regardaient, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut élevé, et une nuée {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}enleva à leurs yeux.
fr.B: Après avoir dit cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut élevé sous leurs yeux, et une nuée {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accueillit, si bien qu’ils ne {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} virent plus.
fr.R: Après avoir dit cela, Jésus a été élevé vers le ciel pendant qu’ils regardaient. Puis un nuage {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a caché, et ils ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont plus vu.

sw.L: Na baada ya kusema mambo haya, huku wakimtazama, aliinuliwa juu, na wingu likamchukua kutoka mbele ya macho yao.
sw.B: Baada ya maneno hayo, aliinuliwa juu wao wakitazama, na wingu likamchukua, hata macho yao yasiweze kumwona tena.
sw.R: Yesu alipomaliza kusema hayo, aliinuliwa juu angani huku wakiangalia. Kisha wingu likamfunika, na hawakuweza kumwona tena.

vi.L: Nói xong những điều ấy, trong khi họ đang nhìn, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được cất lên, và một đám mây tiếp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} khuất khỏi mắt họ.
vi.B: Nói xong những lời ấy, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được cất lên ngay trước mắt họ, và một đám mây tiếp đón {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, khiến họ không còn thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nữa.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói xong thì được cất lên bầu trời trong khi họ đang nhìn theo. Rồi một đám mây che khuất {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và họ không còn thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nữa.

ko.L: 그리고 이 말씀을 하시고 나서, 그들이 보고 있는 가운데 그분이 들려 올라가셨다. 그리고 구름이 그분을 받아 그들의 눈에서 [가렸다].
ko.B: 이 말씀을 하신 뒤에, 그들이 보는 앞에서 예수께서 들려 올라가셨다. 그리고 구름이 예수를 감싸, 그들의 눈에 더 이상 보이지 않게 되었다.
ko.R: 이렇게 말씀하신 뒤에, 예수께서는 사도들이 보는 앞에서 하늘로 들려 올라가셨다. 그러자 구름이 예수를 가렸고, 그들은 더 이상 예수를 볼 수 없었다.

decisions.choice: took him up: the cloud received him and bore him out of sight
decisions.reason: The verb means to take up from beneath, or to receive. The cloud is more than a curtain: it carries him away (compare 1:11, "taken up").

decisions.choice: the cloud: a sign of God's presence
decisions.reason: A cloud marks God's presence at Sinai and over the tent (Exodus 19:9, 40:34) and at Jesus's transfiguration (Luke 9:34-35). In Daniel 7:13 one like a son of man comes with the clouds of heaven to God, and Jesus says he will come back "in a cloud" (Luke 21:27).

decisions.choice: was lifted up: God lifted him
alternatives: he rose by his own act
decisions.reason: The passive leaves God as the one who acts, as in 1:2 and 1:11.

decisions.choice: into the sky
decisions.reason: Readable says where he was lifted, as 1:10 does.

decisions.choice: une nuée (L, B); un nuage (R)
decisions.reason: "Une nuée" is the word French uses for the cloud of God's presence in the Scriptures (m2), and it keeps that echo at Literal and Balanced. Readable says "un nuage", the everyday word.

decisions.choice: "들려 올라가다" for the passive "was lifted up"; "구름이 ... 받아" (L), "감싸" (B), "가렸다" (R)
decisions.reason: God lifted him (meaning decision), so Korean keeps the passive "들리다", as the Korean Luke 24:51 does. The cloud received him and bore him out of sight; each level says it in its own words.

source.text: καὶ ὡς ἀτενίζοντες ἦσαν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν πορευομένου αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο παρειστήκεισαν αὐτοῖς ἐν ἐσθήσεσι λευκαῖς, οἳ καὶ εἶπαν· Ἄνδρες Γαλιλαῖοι, τί ἑστήκατε βλέποντες εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν;

records.literal_gloss: And as gazing they were into the sky, going him, and look, men two stood by them in clothes white, \v 11 who also said, Men Galileans, why do you stand looking into the sky?

en.L: And as they were gazing into the sky while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going, then look, two men stood beside them in white clothing, \v 11 who also said, "Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into the sky?
en.B: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went, they kept their eyes fixed on the sky, and all at once two men dressed in white were there beside them. \v 11 "Men of Galilee," they said, "why stand there gazing up at the sky?
en.R: The apostles were still staring at the sky as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went away. Then suddenly two men wearing white clothes were standing next to them. \v 11 They said, "Men from Galilee, why are you standing here looking at the sky?

es.L: Y como estaban mirando fijamente al cielo mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se iba, entonces, mira, dos hombres se presentaron junto a ellos con ropas blancas, \v 11 los cuales también dijeron: «Hombres galileos, ¿por qué {{plural_you:están|estáis}} de pie mirando al cielo?
es.B: Mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se alejaba, ellos tenían la vista fija en el cielo, y de repente se presentaron junto a ellos dos hombres vestidos de blanco. \v 11 Ellos dijeron: «Hombres de Galilea, ¿por qué {{plural_you:se quedan|os quedáis}} ahí mirando al cielo?
es.R: Los apóstoles seguían mirando al cielo mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se iba. De pronto, dos hombres vestidos de blanco aparecieron a su lado. \v 11 Les dijeron: «Hombres de Galilea, ¿por qué {{plural_you:están|estáis}} aquí de pie mirando al cielo?

fr.L: Et comme ils avaient les yeux fixés vers le ciel pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’en allait, voici que deux hommes se tenaient près d’eux en vêtements blancs, \v 11 qui aussi dirent : « Hommes de Galilée, pourquoi vous tenez-vous [là] à regarder vers le ciel ?
fr.B: Tandis qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’en allait, ils gardaient les yeux fixés sur le ciel, et soudain deux hommes vêtus de blanc se trouvèrent à côté d’eux. \v 11 « Hommes de Galilée, dirent-ils, pourquoi restez-vous là à regarder le ciel ?
fr.R: Les apôtres regardaient encore le ciel pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’en allait. Tout à coup, deux hommes habillés de blanc se sont trouvés à côté d’eux. \v 11 Ils ont dit : « Vous qui venez de Galilée, pourquoi restez-vous ici à regarder le ciel ?

sw.L: Na walipokuwa wakikodolea macho angani, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} akienda, basi tazama, wanaume wawili waliovaa nguo nyeupe walisimama kando yao, \v 11 nao pia walisema, "Wanaume wa Galilaya, kwa nini mnasimama mkiangalia angani?
sw.B: Alipokuwa akienda, wao waliendelea kukaza macho angani, na ghafla wanaume wawili waliovaa nguo nyeupe walikuwa wamesimama kando yao. \v 11 Wakasema, "Wanaume wa Galilaya, kwa nini mnasimama hapo mkiangalia juu angani?
sw.R: Mitume walikuwa bado wakiangalia angani alipokuwa akiondoka. Ghafla wanaume wawili waliovaa nguo nyeupe walisimama karibu nao. \v 11 Wakasema, "Wanaume kutoka Galilaya, kwa nini mmesimama hapa mkiangalia angani?

vi.L: Và khi họ đang chăm chú nhìn lên trời trong lúc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi, thì kìa, có hai người nam mặc áo trắng đứng bên cạnh họ, \v 11 và nói: "Hỡi những người Ga-li-lê, sao các ông đứng nhìn lên trời?
vi.B: Trong khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi lên, họ cứ chăm chú nhìn lên trời; bỗng có hai người nam mặc áo trắng đứng bên cạnh họ. \v 11 Hai người ấy nói: "Hỡi các ông người Ga-li-lê, sao các ông đứng đó nhìn lên trời?
vi.R: Các sứ đồ vẫn còn đang nhìn chăm chú lên bầu trời khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi. Bỗng nhiên có hai người nam mặc áo trắng đứng bên cạnh họ. \v 11 Họ nói: "Này các ông người Ga-li-lê, sao các ông đứng đây nhìn lên bầu trời?

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 가실 때에 그들이 하늘을 뚫어지게 쳐다보고 있었는데, 보라, 흰옷을 입은 두 남자가 그들 곁에 서 있었다. \v 11 그들이 말했다. "갈릴리 사람들아, 왜 하늘을 쳐다보며 서 있느냐?
ko.B: 예수께서 올라가시는 동안 그들이 하늘을 뚫어지게 바라보고 있는데, 갑자기 흰옷을 입은 두 남자가 그들 곁에 서 있었다. \v 11 그들이 말했다. "갈릴리 사람들아, 왜 여기 서서 하늘을 쳐다보고 있느냐?
ko.R: 예수께서 떠나가시는 동안 사도들은 하늘만 쳐다보고 있었다. 그런데 갑자기 흰옷을 입은 두 사람이 그들 곁에 서 있었다. \v 11 그 두 사람이 말했다. "갈릴리에서 온 사람들아, 왜 여기 서서 하늘만 쳐다보고 있느냐?

decisions.choice: two men in white: messengers from God, angels
decisions.reason: Luke tells of "two men" in dazzling clothes at the empty tomb (Luke 24:4), whom the women later call angels (Luke 24:23). White clothing marks heavenly beings (Luke 9:29-30).

decisions.choice: the sky: the word means both sky and heaven
alternatives: heaven, as a place beyond the sky
decisions.reason: They are looking up at the sky where he went; the same word is "heaven" in 1:11, where he has gone. Greek has one word for both.

decisions.choice: look: a word that points to something sudden
decisions.reason: The word calls attention to what comes next, here the men who are suddenly there.

decisions.choice: men of Galilee: the apostles, who came from Galilee
decisions.reason: Jesus called his first followers in Galilee (Luke 5:1-11). Galileans could be known by their speech (Mark 14:70).

decisions.choice: look (L); all at once (B); suddenly (R)
decisions.reason: Modern English does not say "behold". Literal keeps a word that points; Balanced and Readable show the surprise in the wording.

decisions.choice: the apostles
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are.

decisions.choice: angani (here); mbinguni (1:11, "into heaven")
decisions.reason: The Greek word means both sky and heaven (meaning decision m2). Swahili has two words, as English does: "anga" where the apostles stare up at the sky, "mbingu" where Jesus is taken into heaven, following the English.

decisions.choice: The two men in white call the apostles "các ông": "Hỡi những người Ga-li-lê" (L), "Hỡi các ông người Ga-li-lê" (B), "Này các ông người Ga-li-lê" (R)
decisions.reason: The messengers from God (meaning decision) speak to grown men with the courteous "các ông", as the angel in the Vietnamese Luke 1:13 speaks to Zechariah as "ông".

decisions.choice: "kìa" (L); "bỗng" (B); "Bỗng nhiên" (R) for "look"
decisions.reason: As in the English, Literal keeps the pointing word and the other levels turn it into "suddenly".

decisions.choice: the two men speak to the apostles in 해라체 ("사람들아", "-느냐"), as the angels do in the Korean Luke 24:5
decisions.reason: They are messengers from God (meaning decision); the Korean Luke has angels speak to people in the plain style (Luke 1:13; 24:5). "두 남자" (L, B), as in the Korean Luke 24:4.

decisions.choice: "보라" (L), "갑자기" (B, R) for idou
decisions.reason: As the Korean Luke: Literal keeps "보라", Balanced and Readable say what it signals, as the English does.

source.text: οὗτος ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὁ ἀναλημφθεὶς ἀφ’ ὑμῶν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν οὕτως ἐλεύσεται ὃν τρόπον ἐθεάσασθε αὐτὸν πορευόμενον εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.

records.literal_gloss: This the Jesus the having been taken up from you into the heaven so will come in which manner you saw him going into the heaven.

en.L: This Jesus, who has been taken up from you into heaven, will so come in the manner [in] which you saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} going into heaven."
en.B: This Jesus has been taken up from you into heaven, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come in the very way you saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} leave for heaven."
en.R: Jesus has been taken away from you into heaven. But one day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come back. He will come in the same way you saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} go."

es.L: Este Jesús, que ha sido llevado arriba de entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} al cielo, vendrá así, del mismo modo en que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:vieron|visteis}} irse al cielo».
es.B: Este Jesús, que ha sido llevado de entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} al cielo, vendrá de la misma manera en que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:vieron|visteis}} partir hacia el cielo».
es.R: Jesús ha sido llevado al cielo, lejos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Pero un día volverá. Vendrá de la misma manera en que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:vieron|visteis}} irse».

fr.L: Ce Jésus, qui a été enlevé d’auprès de vous au ciel, viendra ainsi, de la même manière que vous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avez vu s’en aller au ciel. »
fr.B: Ce Jésus a été enlevé d’auprès de vous au ciel, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} viendra exactement comme vous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avez vu partir pour le ciel. »
fr.R: Jésus vous a été enlevé et emporté au ciel. Mais un jour, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} reviendra. Il reviendra de la même façon que vous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avez vu partir. »

sw.L: Yesu huyu aliyeondolewa kwenu na kupandishwa mbinguni atakuja kwa namna ileile ambayo mmemwona akienda mbinguni."
sw.B: Yesu huyu aliyechukuliwa kutoka kwenu kwenda mbinguni atakuja kwa namna ileile mliyomwona akiondoka kwenda mbinguni."
sw.R: Yesu amechukuliwa kutoka kwenu kwenda mbinguni. Lakini siku moja atarudi. Atakuja kwa namna ileile mliyomwona akienda."

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu này, Đấng đã được cất lên khỏi các ông vào trời, cũng sẽ đến theo cách như các ông đã thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi vào trời."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu này đã được cất lên khỏi các ông vào trời, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ trở lại đúng như cách các ông đã thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên trời."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu đã được đem lên trời, rời khỏi các ông. Nhưng một ngày kia {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ trở lại. Ngài sẽ trở lại giống như cách các ông đã thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ra đi."

ko.L: 너희에게서 하늘로 들려 올라가신 이 예수께서는, 너희가 그분이 하늘로 가시는 것을 본 그대로 그렇게 오실 것이다."
ko.B: 너희를 떠나 하늘로 들려 올라가신 이 예수께서는, 너희가 본 대로 하늘로 가신 그 모습 그대로 다시 오실 것이다."
ko.R: 예수께서는 너희를 떠나 하늘로 올라가셨다. 그러나 언젠가 다시 오실 것이다. 너희가 본 것처럼, 하늘로 가신 모습 그대로 오실 것이다."

decisions.choice: he will come in the same way: as he went, in a cloud and seen, he will return
alternatives: his coming in the Spirit at Pentecost
decisions.reason: He went up in a cloud while they watched (1:9); Jesus said the Son of Man would come "in a cloud with power and great glory" (Luke 21:27).

decisions.choice: this Jesus: the same person, not another
decisions.reason: The words stress that the one who returns is the Jesus they knew.

decisions.choice: one day; come back
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the coming is still future and is a return.

decisions.choice: the two men speak of Jesus with the honorific ("올라가신", "오실")
decisions.reason: Messengers from God speak of Jesus with respect, as the angels of the Korean Luke 24:5-7 do of "살아 계신 분".

source.text: Τότε ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἀπὸ ὄρους τοῦ καλουμένου Ἐλαιῶνος, ὅ ἐστιν ἐγγὺς Ἰερουσαλὴμ σαββάτου ἔχον ὁδόν.

records.literal_gloss: Then they returned to Jerusalem from mountain the called Olive Grove, which is near Jerusalem, of a Sabbath having a way.

en.L: Then they returned to Jerusalem from [the] mountain called Olive Grove, which is near Jerusalem, a Sabbath's journey away.
en.B: Then they went back to Jerusalem from the hill called the Mount of Olives. It lies close to the city, {{units:about half a mile|a Sabbath day's walk}} away.
en.R: Then the apostles walked back to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives. It was only {{units:about half a mile|a Sabbath day's walk}} from the city.

es.L: Entonces regresaron a Jerusalén desde [el] monte llamado Olivar, que está cerca de Jerusalén, a un camino de sábado.
es.B: Luego volvieron a Jerusalén desde el cerro llamado monte de los Olivos. Está cerca de la ciudad, a {{units:menos de un kilómetro|un camino de sábado}}.
es.R: Entonces los apóstoles regresaron caminando a Jerusalén desde el monte de los Olivos. Estaba a solo {{units:menos de un kilómetro|un camino de sábado}} de la ciudad.

fr.L: Alors ils retournèrent à Jérusalem depuis la montagne appelée Oliveraie, qui est près de Jérusalem, à [une distance d’]un chemin de sabbat.
fr.B: Alors ils revinrent à Jérusalem depuis la colline qu’on appelle le mont des Oliviers. Elle se trouve près de la ville, à {{units:environ un kilomètre|une marche de sabbat}}.
fr.R: Puis les apôtres sont rentrés à pied à Jérusalem depuis le mont des Oliviers. Cet endroit n’était qu’à {{units:environ un kilomètre|une marche de sabbat}} de la ville.

sw.L: Ndipo walirudi Yerusalemu kutoka mlima uitwao Shamba la Mizeituni, ulio karibu na Yerusalemu, umbali wa safari ya Sabato.
sw.B: Kisha walirudi Yerusalemu kutoka kilima kiitwacho Mlima wa Mizeituni. Kiko karibu na mji, {{units:chini ya kilomita moja|mwendo wa siku ya Sabato}} kutoka huko.
sw.R: Kisha mitume walitembea kurudi Yerusalemu kutoka Mlima wa Mizeituni. Ulikuwa {{units:chini ya kilomita moja|mwendo wa siku ya Sabato}} tu kutoka mjini.

vi.L: Bấy giờ họ trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem từ núi gọi là [núi] Ô-li-ve, là núi gần Giê-ru-sa-lem, cách một quãng đường ngày Sa-bát.
vi.B: Rồi họ từ ngọn đồi gọi là núi Ô-li-ve trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem. Núi này ở gần thành, cách {{units:chừng một cây số|một quãng đường ngày Sa-bát}}.
vi.R: Sau đó các sứ đồ đi bộ từ núi Ô-li-ve trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem. Núi ấy chỉ cách thành {{units:chừng một cây số|một quãng đường ngày Sa-bát}}.

ko.L: 그때에 그들은 올리브 밭이라고 불리는 산에서 예루살렘으로 돌아왔다. 그 산은 예루살렘에서 가까워, 안식일에 [걸을 수 있는] 길만큼 떨어져 있다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 그들은 올리브 산이라고 하는 산에서 예루살렘으로 돌아왔다. 그 산은 예루살렘에서 가까워, {{units:800미터쯤|안식일에 걸어도 되는 거리만큼}} 떨어져 있다.
ko.R: 사도들은 올리브 산에서 걸어서 예루살렘으로 돌아왔다. 그 산은 예루살렘에서 {{units:800미터쯤|안식일에 걸어도 되는 거리만큼}}밖에 떨어져 있지 않았다.

decisions.choice: a Sabbath day's journey: the distance a Jew could walk on the Sabbath, about 2,000 cubits
decisions.reason: Jewish teachers set this limit from Exodus 16:29 and the 2,000 cubits of Numbers 35:5. It is about 1,000 yards, a little over half a mile. Luke means only that the hill is close; it need not have been a Sabbath.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives: the ridge east of Jerusalem, across the Kidron valley
decisions.reason: Luke 24:50 places the parting near Bethany, which is on the far slope of the same ridge. Zechariah 14:4 pictures the Lord standing on this mountain on his day.

decisions.choice: about half a mile, with "a Sabbath day's walk" as the alternative
decisions.reason: A modern measure is the default and the original unit the setting, as everywhere. Literal keeps the original.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives
decisions.reason: The name means an olive grove. English knows the place as the Mount of Olives, as Luke himself calls it in Luke 19:29 and 22:39.

decisions.choice: {{units:menos de un kilómetro|un camino de sábado}}
decisions.reason: Spanish readers measure in metres and kilometres, so the default is metric where the English gives "about half a mile". The distance a Jew could walk on the Sabbath was about 2,000 cubits (meaning decision m1), a little under a kilometre; the alternative keeps the Greek measure. Literal keeps the Greek wording, as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: {{units:environ un kilomètre|une marche de sabbat}}
alternatives: "environ huit cents mètres" (half a mile, as the English)
decisions.reason: French defaults to metric. A Sabbath day's journey was about 2,000 cubits, roughly 900 metres, so "environ un kilomètre" is the honest round figure; the English says "about half a mile". The original unit is the alternative, and Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: {{units:chini ya kilomita moja|mwendo wa siku ya Sabato}}
decisions.reason: Swahili measures in metric units, so the default is "under a kilometre" where the English gives "about half a mile": the Sabbath limit was about 2,000 cubits (meaning decision m1). The alternative keeps the Greek measure. This differs from the English US units.

decisions.choice: {{units:chừng một cây số|một quãng đường ngày Sa-bát}} (B, R); Literal keeps "một quãng đường ngày Sa-bát"
decisions.reason: The style guide gives metric measures by default, with the original measure as the alternative; the English gives US units. A Sabbath day's walk was about 2,000 cubits (meaning decision), somewhat under a kilometre.

decisions.choice: "núi Ô-li-ve" for the Mount of Olives, as in the Vietnamese Luke 19:29
decisions.reason: The Greek name means "Olive Grove"; Vietnamese readers know the place as "núi Ô-li-ve", the form of the Gospels.

decisions.choice: {{units:800미터쯤|안식일에 걸어도 되는 거리만큼}} (B, R); Literal keeps the Sabbath's journey
decisions.reason: The distance a Jew could walk on the Sabbath was about 2,000 cubits (meaning decision). Korean gives the metric distance by default and the original measure as the alternative (style guide, section 7), where the English gives US units; the particle after it fits both forms.

decisions.choice: "올리브 밭이라고 불리는 산" (L); "올리브 산" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek name, "Olive Grove"; Balanced and Readable say "올리브 산", the form of the Korean Luke 19:29 and 21:37 (style guide, Settled: the modern word over "감람").

source.text: καὶ ὅτε εἰσῆλθον, εἰς τὸ ὑπερῷον ἀνέβησαν οὗ ἦσαν καταμένοντες, ὅ τε Πέτρος καὶ Ἰωάννης καὶ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἀνδρέας, Φίλιππος καὶ Θωμᾶς, Βαρθολομαῖος καὶ Μαθθαῖος, Ἰάκωβος Ἁλφαίου καὶ Σίμων ὁ ζηλωτὴς καὶ Ἰούδας Ἰακώβου.

records.literal_gloss: And when they entered, into the upper room they went up where they were staying, both Peter and John and James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James of Alphaeus and Simon the Zealot and Judas of James.

en.L: And when they had entered [the city], they went up into the upper room where they were staying: Peter and John and James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James [son] of Alphaeus and Simon the Zealot and Judas [son] of James.
en.B: Back in the city, they climbed to the upstairs room where they had been lodging. Peter was there, with John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James.
en.R: When they got back to the city, they went up to the room upstairs where they were staying. These were the apostles: Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas the son of James.

es.L: Y cuando entraron [en la ciudad], subieron al aposento alto donde se alojaban: Pedro y Juan y Santiago y Andrés, Felipe y Tomás, Bartolomé y Mateo, Santiago [hijo] de Alfeo y Simón el Zelote y Judas [hijo] de Santiago.
es.B: Ya en la ciudad, subieron a la habitación del piso de arriba donde se estaban hospedando. Allí estaban Pedro, Juan, Santiago y Andrés, Felipe y Tomás, Bartolomé y Mateo, Santiago hijo de Alfeo, Simón el Zelote y Judas hijo de Santiago.
es.R: Cuando volvieron a la ciudad, subieron al cuarto del piso de arriba donde se estaban quedando. Estos eran los apóstoles: Pedro, Juan, Santiago, Andrés, Felipe, Tomás, Bartolomé, Mateo, Santiago el hijo de Alfeo, Simón el Zelote y Judas el hijo de Santiago.

fr.L: Et quand ils furent entrés [dans la ville], ils montèrent dans la chambre haute où ils séjournaient : Pierre et Jean et Jacques et André, Philippe et Thomas, Barthélemy et Matthieu, Jacques [fils] d’Alphée et Simon le Zélote et Jude [fils] de Jacques.
fr.B: De retour dans la ville, ils montèrent à la pièce de l’étage où ils logeaient. Il y avait là Pierre, avec Jean, Jacques et André, Philippe et Thomas, Barthélemy et Matthieu, Jacques fils d’Alphée, Simon le Zélote et Jude fils de Jacques.
fr.R: Quand ils sont arrivés dans la ville, ils sont montés dans la pièce à l’étage où ils logeaient. Voici qui étaient les apôtres : Pierre, Jean, Jacques, André, Philippe, Thomas, Barthélemy, Matthieu, Jacques le fils d’Alphée, Simon le Zélote et Jude le fils de Jacques.

sw.L: Na walipokwisha kuingia [mjini], walipanda kwenda chumba cha juu walimokuwa wakikaa: Petro na Yohana na Yakobo na Andrea, Filipo na Tomaso, Bartholomayo na Mathayo, Yakobo [mwana] wa Alfayo na Simoni Mzelote na Yuda [mwana] wa Yakobo.
sw.B: Walipofika mjini, walipanda kwenda chumba cha ghorofani walimokuwa wakikaa. Walikuwepo Petro, Yohana, Yakobo na Andrea, Filipo na Tomaso, Bartholomayo na Mathayo, Yakobo mwana wa Alfayo, Simoni Mzelote, na Yuda mwana wa Yakobo.
sw.R: Waliporudi mjini, walipanda kwenda chumba cha juu ya nyumba walimokuwa wakikaa. Hawa ndio waliokuwa mitume: Petro, Yohana, Yakobo, Andrea, Filipo, Tomaso, Bartholomayo, Mathayo, Yakobo mwana wa Alfayo, Simoni Mzelote, na Yuda mwana wa Yakobo.

vi.L: Và khi đã vào [thành], họ lên phòng cao, là nơi họ đang ở: Phi-e-rơ và Giăng và Gia-cơ và Anh-rê, Phi-líp và Thô-ma, Ba-thê-lê-my và Ma-thi-ơ, Gia-cơ [con] của A-phê và Si-môn người Xê-lốt và Giu-đa [con] của Gia-cơ.
vi.B: Vào đến thành, họ lên căn phòng trên lầu, nơi họ vẫn ở. Có mặt ở đó là Phi-e-rơ, cùng với Giăng, Gia-cơ và Anh-rê, Phi-líp và Thô-ma, Ba-thê-lê-my và Ma-thi-ơ, Gia-cơ con A-phê, Si-môn người Xê-lốt, và Giu-đa con Gia-cơ.
vi.R: Khi về đến thành, họ lên căn phòng trên lầu, nơi họ đang ở. Đây là các sứ đồ: Phi-e-rơ, Giăng, Gia-cơ, Anh-rê, Phi-líp, Thô-ma, Ba-thê-lê-my, Ma-thi-ơ, Gia-cơ con của A-phê, Si-môn "người Nhiệt Thành", và Giu-đa con của Gia-cơ.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 [성에] 들어가서, 묵고 있던 다락방으로 올라갔다. [그들은] 베드로와 요한과 야고보와 안드레, 빌립과 도마, 바돌로매와 마태, 알패오의 [아들] 야고보와 열심당원 시몬과 야고보의 [아들] 유다였다.
ko.B: 그들은 성안으로 들어가서, 머물고 있던 다락방으로 올라갔다. 거기에는 베드로와 요한과 야고보와 안드레, 빌립과 도마, 바돌로매와 마태, 알패오의 아들 야고보와 열심당원 시몬과 야고보의 아들 유다가 있었다.
ko.R: 사도들은 성안으로 돌아와서, 묵고 있던 집의 위층 방으로 올라갔다. 사도들은 베드로, 요한, 야고보, 안드레, 빌립, 도마, 바돌로매, 마태, 알패오의 아들 야고보, 열심당원 시몬, 야고보의 아들 유다였다.

decisions.choice: the upper room: a room on the upper floor or roof of a house
decisions.reason: Such rooms could be large (20:8-9). It may be the room of the last supper, but Luke uses a different word there (Luke 22:12), so this is not certain.

decisions.choice: the Zealot: one known for zeal
decisions.reason: Luke 6:15 also calls him "the Zealot". The word means someone zealous, for God and the law. It may also mean he had belonged to those who wanted to throw off Roman rule; the Zealot party is known by that name only some decades later.

decisions.choice: Judas of James: Judas son of James
decisions.reason: Greek often names a man by his father this way, as in "James of Alphaeus" just before. Some read "brother of James", taking him to be the author of the letter of Jude, who calls himself "brother of James" (Jude 1). He is not Judas Iscariot (John 14:22).

decisions.choice: where they were staying: the place they were living or regularly met
decisions.reason: The verb describes an ongoing stay, and 1:14 shows them continuing there.

decisions.choice: [the city]; [son]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets what English needs to make sense of the verb and of the names. Balanced and Readable say it as English would.

decisions.choice: Santiago for every James; Simón el Zelote
decisions.reason: As in Luke 6:14-16: one form for every James keeps it plain that Judas's father bears the same name, and Luke uses the Greek word "Zealot" itself (meaning decision m2), so every level says "Zelote".

decisions.choice: Jude [fils] de Jacques
decisions.reason: The Greek name is the same as that of Judas Iscariot (1:16). French usage calls this apostle "Jude", which keeps the two men apart for the reader without changing the name's meaning.

decisions.choice: Simoni Mzelote
decisions.reason: As in Luke 6:15: Luke uses the Greek word "Zealot" itself (meaning decision m2), so every level says "Mzelote".

decisions.choice: The apostles' names as in the Vietnamese Luke 6:14-16; "người Xê-lốt" (L, B), "người Nhiệt Thành" (R)
decisions.reason: The Protestant forms are settled. Readable translates "Zealot" as the Vietnamese Luke's Readable does.

decisions.choice: the apostles' names in the forms of the Korean Luke 6:14-16 ("바돌로매", "알패오", "열심당원 시몬"); "다락방" (L, B), "위층 방" (R)
decisions.reason: The names as the Korean Luke gives them, so the list reads the same in both volumes. "다락방" is the Korean Luke 22:12's word for the upper room; Readable says plainly that it was upstairs, as the English Readable does.

source.text: οὗτοι πάντες ἦσαν προσκαρτεροῦντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν τῇ προσευχῇ σὺν γυναιξὶν καὶ Μαριὰμ τῇ μητρὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ σὺν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: These all were continuing with one mind in the prayer with women and Mary the mother of the Jesus and with the brothers of him.

en.L: These all were devoting themselves with one mind to prayer, with [the] women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers.
en.B: All of these were devoted to prayer and of one mind in it. With them were the women, Mary the mother of Jesus, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers.
en.R: They all met often and prayed with one heart. The women who had followed Jesus were with them too, and so were Mary, the mother of Jesus, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers.

es.L: Todos estos se dedicaban con un mismo ánimo a la oración, junto con [las] mujeres y María la madre de Jesús, y con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanos.
es.B: Todos ellos se entregaban de lleno a la oración, con un mismo sentir. Los acompañaban las mujeres, María la madre de Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanos.
es.R: Todos se reunían a menudo y oraban con un mismo corazón. También estaban con ellos las mujeres que habían seguido a Jesús, y además María, la madre de Jesús, y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanos.

fr.L: Tous ceux-là, unanimes, persévéraient dans la prière, avec des femmes et Marie la mère de Jésus, et avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} frères.
fr.B: Tous étaient assidus à la prière, unis dans un même esprit. Avec eux se trouvaient les femmes, Marie, la mère de Jésus, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} frères.
fr.R: Ils se réunissaient souvent et priaient tous ensemble, d’un même cœur. Les femmes qui avaient suivi Jésus étaient là aussi, ainsi que Marie, la mère de Jésus, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} frères.

sw.L: Hawa wote walikuwa wakijitoa kwa nia moja kwa maombi, pamoja na wanawake na Mariamu, mama wa Yesu, na pamoja na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.B: Wote hao walijitoa kwa bidii kwa maombi, wakiwa na nia moja. Pamoja nao walikuwepo wale wanawake, Mariamu mama wa Yesu, na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.R: Wote walikutana mara kwa mara na kuomba kwa moyo mmoja. Wanawake waliokuwa wamemfuata Yesu nao walikuwa pamoja nao, na pia Mariamu, mama wa Yesu, na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.

vi.L: Tất cả những người này đều một lòng chuyên tâm cầu nguyện, cùng với [các] phụ nữ, với Ma-ri, mẹ của Đức Giê-xu, và với các anh em của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Tất cả những người ấy đều một lòng chuyên tâm cầu nguyện. Cùng ở với họ có các phụ nữ, Ma-ri mẹ của Đức Giê-xu, và các anh em của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Họ thường xuyên nhóm lại và cùng một lòng cầu nguyện. Những phụ nữ đã theo Đức Giê-xu cũng ở với họ, cùng với Ma-ri, mẹ của Đức Giê-xu, và các anh em của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 이 사람들은 모두 여자들과 예수의 어머니 마리아와 그분의 형제들과 함께, 한마음으로 기도에 힘쓰고 있었다.
ko.B: 이들은 모두 한마음이 되어 기도에 힘썼다. 여자들과 예수의 어머니 마리아와 예수의 형제들도 그들과 함께 있었다.
ko.R: 그들은 모두 자주 모여서 한마음으로 기도했다. 예수를 따르던 여자들도 함께 있었다. 예수의 어머니 마리아와 예수의 형제들도 함께 있었다.

decisions.choice: with one mind: united in purpose, together
decisions.reason: This is a favorite word of Luke's for the believers' unity (2:46, 4:24, 5:12).

decisions.choice: devoting themselves to prayer: they kept at it
decisions.reason: The verb means to keep at something without giving up, the same word as in 2:42. "The prayer" may include the set hours of prayer (3:1).

decisions.choice: women: the women who followed Jesus from Galilee
decisions.reason: Luke has told of women who traveled with Jesus and supported him (Luke 8:2-3) and who saw the cross, the tomb and the empty tomb (Luke 23:49, 23:55-24:10). The Greek has no article, but these are most likely the women meant.

decisions.choice: his brothers: the brothers of Jesus named in Mark 6:3
decisions.reason: Mark 6:3 names James, Joses, Judas and Simon. They did not believe in him during his ministry (John 7:5); the risen Jesus appeared to James (1 Corinthians 15:7), who later leads in Jerusalem (Acts 15:13). The word is the usual one for brothers; some Christian traditions take them to be close relatives instead.

decisions.choice: the women who had followed Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says which women, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: "các anh em của Ngài" for his brothers, with no gender span, as in the Vietnamese Luke 8:19
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must otherwise say whether a brother is older ("anh") or younger ("em"); "anh em" leaves that open, as the Greek does. These are his brothers by family, not believers, so there is no setting span.

decisions.choice: "형제들", not "동생들", with no gender span
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Luke 8:19 and Mark 6:3: "동생들" would decide that they were younger, which the text does not say. Specific men are meant (meaning decision).

source.text: Καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ἀναστὰς Πέτρος ἐν μέσῳ τῶν ἀδελφῶν εἶπεν ἦν τε ὄχλος ὀνομάτων ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ὡς ἑκατὸν εἴκοσι·

records.literal_gloss: And in the days these having stood up Peter in middle of the brothers said (was and crowd of names at the same about 120):

en.L: And in these days Peter stood up in [the] middle of the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} and said (and there was a crowd of names together, about 120):
en.B: In those days Peter rose to speak among the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, a crowd of about 120 people gathered in one place.
en.R: During those days, the followers of Jesus met together. There were about 120 of them. Peter stood up in front of the group and spoke.

es.L: Y en estos días Pedro se levantó en medio de los hermanos y dijo (y había una multitud de nombres reunidos, como ciento veinte):
es.B: En aquellos días, Pedro se puso de pie para hablar entre los hermanos, un grupo de unas ciento veinte personas reunidas en un mismo lugar.
es.R: Por esos días, los discípulos de Jesús se reunieron. Eran unos ciento veinte. Pedro se puso de pie delante del grupo y habló.

fr.L: Et en ces jours-là, Pierre se leva au milieu des {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} et dit (il y avait là une foule de noms réunis, environ cent vingt) :
fr.B: En ces jours-là, Pierre prit la parole au milieu des {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, une foule d’environ cent vingt personnes réunies au même endroit.
fr.R: À cette époque, ceux qui suivaient Jésus se réunissaient. Ils étaient environ cent vingt. Pierre s’est levé devant le groupe et il a parlé.

sw.L: Na katika siku hizi Petro alisimama katikati ya ndugu akasema (na palikuwa na umati wa majina pamoja, kama mia moja na ishirini):
sw.B: Katika siku hizo Petro alisimama kuzungumza kati ya ndugu, kundi la watu wapatao mia moja na ishirini waliokusanyika mahali pamoja.
sw.R: Katika siku hizo, wafuasi wa Yesu walikutana pamoja. Walikuwa watu wapatao mia moja na ishirini. Petro alisimama mbele ya kundi hilo akazungumza.

vi.L: Trong những ngày ấy, Phi-e-rơ đứng dậy giữa các {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} và nói (lúc ấy có một đám đông chừng một trăm hai mươi người nhóm lại):
vi.B: Trong những ngày ấy, Phi-e-rơ đứng lên nói giữa các {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, lúc ấy có chừng một trăm hai mươi người đang nhóm lại tại một chỗ.
vi.R: Trong những ngày ấy, những người theo Đức Giê-xu nhóm lại với nhau. Có chừng một trăm hai mươi người. Phi-e-rơ đứng lên trước mọi người và nói:

ko.L: 그리고 이 무렵에 베드로가 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들 가운데 일어나서 말했다. (모인 무리의 수는 이름으로 백이십쯤 되었다.)
ko.B: 그 무렵에 베드로가 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들 가운데서 일어나 말했다. 그 자리에는 백이십 명쯤 되는 사람들이 모여 있었다.
ko.R: 그 무렵 예수를 따르는 사람들이 함께 모였다. 모두 백이십 명쯤 되었다. 베드로가 그들 앞에서 일어나 말했다.

decisions.choice: the brothers: the believers, men and women
decisions.reason: "Brothers" is the common word for fellow believers in Acts. The women and Mary have just been named among them (1:14), and the group numbers 120.

decisions.choice: a crowd of names: a number of people
decisions.reason: "Names" stands for persons, as in Revelation 3:4.

decisions.choice: the number is an aside before Peter's words
decisions.reason: Luke breaks into his sentence to give the size of the group.

decisions.choice: brothers and sisters, with "brothers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word here means men and women together, as the meaning note explains, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: the followers of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says who these brothers and sisters are. It reorders the sentence so that Peter's words follow at once.

decisions.choice: los hermanos, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The believers were men and women (meaning decision m1), and Spanish "hermanos" already takes in the sisters, so the English gender setting has no Spanish counterpart, as in Romans and Philippians. The same in 1:16 and through the book.

decisions.choice: ndugu, with no gender span
